open_points.subject: system_clock public operation surface
open_points.text: “One public operation per State 3 capability (100 …)” conflicts with the newly added `system_clock` candidate public capabilities `utc_now` and `monotonic_seconds`, for which State 5 defines no `public_op` sections.
open_points.question: Are `utc_now` and `monotonic_seconds` public module operations, and if so what are their exact callers, inputs, outputs, errors and effects; if not, how may the time-consuming modules access the only permitted clock source?
options: Add both operations to State 5 and increase the operation count to 102.
Treat both capabilities as private implementation details and state the permitted public access mechanism.
Replace them with a different single public clock interface and specify its contract.
open_points.default_guess: Add `utc_now()` returning an offset-naive UTC datetime and `monotonic_seconds()` returning a float, with the modules whose `Knows` sections name `system_clock` as callers.

witness.initial: State 6 is being generated from the accepted texts after `system_clock` has been added to State 3.
events: One implementer follows State 3 and exposes `utc_now` and `monotonic_seconds` for consumer modules.
Another implementer follows State 5's complete 100-operation catalogue and treats the clock functions as private or omits them.
outcomes: Time-consuming modules import and call two defined cross-module operations.
The same modules either cannot obtain time through a declared operation or use an undeclared/private mechanism.
witness.observer: The State 6 contract author, generated dependency graph, and module-level tests.

open_points.subject: A28 clock-read cardinality
open_points.text: The change says the wall and elapsed clocks take “one reading per request”, while the existing rule says “An operation reads the clock once”, the new module says “One wall reading per call” and “one elapsed reading per call”, and the change says “each read” remains at the same point of the same operation.
open_points.question: Does “request” mean one HTTP request, one public operation, or one call to `system_clock`; in particular, must authorization, the owning use case, and `append_audit` share one wall reading or take their own readings?
options: One wall reading is shared by every operation executed for one HTTP request.
Each public operation takes its own reading; one HTTP request may therefore read several times.
Each direct call to `system_clock` reads once, with callers independently deciding how many calls an operation makes.
open_points.default_guess: Interpret “request” as a call to the clock source and preserve one wall reading per operation, with `append_audit` taking its separately specified reading.

witness.initial: An active staff session exists, and a project has a section whose progress can be changed; a controllable clock returns successive instants T1, T2 and T3.
events: Staff sends one authenticated request to update section progress.
Session resolution compares expiry with the current time.
outcomes: Under one-reading-per-HTTP-request, all comparisons and both stored timestamps use T1.
Under one-reading-per-operation/call, session resolution uses T1, progress uses T2, and the audit writer uses T3.
witness.observer: A reader of the persisted progress and audit rows, and a focused clock test.
